sourceChecks.title: Symptom improvement in children with autism spectrum disorder following bumetanide administration is associated with decreased GABA/glutamate ratios
sourceChecks.excerpt: the bumetanide group showed significant reduction in symptom severity
sourceChecks.paraphrase: 83-child randomized treated-versus-no-bumetanide study reported three-month symptom-score changes associated with GABA/Glx ratio changes. This is short-term association in one study, not a universal ASD mechanism or cure.
sourceChecks.limitations: Small, not double-blind placebo-controlled confirmation; one treatment and short duration do not show full normalization or one cause for ASD.

sourceChecks.title: Trial of Erythropoietin for Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy in Newborns
sourceChecks.excerpt: did not result in a lower risk of death or neurodevelopmental impairment
sourceChecks.paraphrase: In a randomized trial of 501 infants with moderate/severe HIE, erythropoietin added to therapeutic hypothermia did not reduce death/neurodevelopmental impairment and was associated with more serious adverse events.
sourceChecks.limitations: This tests one adjunct and does not measure brain regeneration as a complete capability.

sourceChecks.title: Childhood Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Treatment (PDQ®)
sourceChecks.locator: Relapsed or refractory B-ALL; CAR T cell therapy sections around 2828–2837 and 2868–2883
sourceChecks.excerpt: U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval of tisagenlecleucel for children with multiply relapsed or refractory B-ALL
sourceChecks.paraphrase: NCI PDQ summarizes CAR-T activity in selected relapsed/refractory B-ALL, including remission rates, but also relapses and persistent event-free-survival limits.
sourceChecks.limitations: Official evidence synthesis, not a new primary trial; only a subtype/setting, not all childhood cancers or single-course non-toxic cure.

sourceChecks.title: Evidence Base for 2022 Updated Recommendations for a Safe Infant Sleeping Environment to Reduce the Risk of Sleep-Related Infant Deaths
sourceChecks.excerpt: making identification of a single cause or universal sequence of mechanisms for sudden death extremely challenging.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: AAP evidence review describes a multifactorial triple-risk model and says a single cause/universal mechanism is hard to identify.
sourceChecks.limitations: Review supports background/goal, not a definitive causal mechanism or preventive intervention that makes incidence near zero.

sourceChecks.title: Stem Cell-Derived, Fully Differentiated Islets for Type 1 Diabetes
sourceChecks.excerpt: Ten of the 12 participants (83%) had insulin independence
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Interim phase 1–2 adult study: 10/12 full-dose recipients were insulin-independent at day 365; all received immunosuppressive therapy.
sourceChecks.limitations: Participants were 18–65 years old, study was small/short and ongoing; does not establish pediatric use, immune tolerance, prevention, permanent cure, or safety without immunosuppression. Adults aged18–65, immunosuppression in every participant, interim non-prespecified analyses, small cohort; not pediatric immunosuppression-free prevention/cure.

sourceChecks.title: Expanded Access use of Intravenous Gene Transfer with AAV9-GLB1 in a Juvenile GM1 Gangliosidosis Participant
sourceChecks.excerpt: A single intravenous administration of AAV9-GLB1
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A medRxiv preprint reports expanded-access one-patient AAV9-GLB1 treatment for juvenile GM1 gangliosidosis with biochemical/neuroimaging changes and some clinical improvements.
sourceChecks.limitations: Single-patient preprint, not peer-reviewed in the retrieved record; one disorder does not support a universal newborn platform or safety across metabolic diseases. Unreviewed author preprint, one child without concurrent control; attributed observations do not prove general clinical efficacy.

sourceChecks.title: Prenatal Repair of Myelomeningocele and School-age Functional Outcomes
sourceChecks.excerpt: There was no significant difference between surgery groups in overall adaptive behavior
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Follow-up of randomized MOMS trial found selected mobility/function and shunt-related advantages of prenatal myelomeningocele repair, without significant overall adaptive behavior difference.
sourceChecks.limitations: Surgical and condition-specific; does not establish a non-invasive platform, correction of multiple anomaly classes, or complete prevention of disability.

sourceChecks.title: Donor antigen-specific regulatory T cell administration to recipients of live donor kidneys: A ONE Study consortium pilot trial
sourceChecks.excerpt: Complete immunosuppression withdrawal was not permitted
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Adult three-recipient phaseI/II donor-reactive Treg pilot reports no rejection episodes and long-term tacrolimus monotherapy after reduction of other drugs. Complete immunosuppression withdrawal was prohibited; uncontrolled feasibility/safety evidence only.
sourceChecks.limitations: Not pediatric or multiple-organ evidence; complete immunosuppression withdrawal was explicitly not permitted, and study was not powered for comparative rejection outcomes.

sourceChecks.title: Advancing Transplantation Outcomes in Children (CTOT-41)
sourceChecks.excerpt: This is a pediatric kidney transplant study comparing the safety and efficacy
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Ongoing pediatric kidney-transplant study compares two immunosuppressive regimens, with planned enrollment of 200 and primary follow-up of 12–24 months.
sourceChecks.limitations: Registry summary shows a trial in progress, not donor-specific tolerance or completed outcomes.

sourceChecks.title: Tisagenlecleucel in Children and Young Adults with B-Cell Lymphoblastic Leukemia
sourceChecks.paraphrase: NCI citation followed to matching primary trial metadata; result passage follow-up returned CAPTCHA and direct resolved URL timed out. No primary result inferred from search or metadata.
sourceChecks.limitations: Does not substantiate the full original aspiration or its impact forecast.

items.corrections: One small pediatric study reported short-term symptom-score and GABA/Glx changes with bumetanide, while its introduction notes that ASD mechanisms remain largely unknown.
A 501-infant randomized trial tested adjunct erythropoietin with standard cooling and found no lower death/neurodevelopmental-impairment risk; full functional regeneration remains unestablished.

Official NCI treatment review summarizes indication-specific CAR-T trials and approval, but is a secondary evidence synthesis. The linked primary trial record could not be independently read after CAPTCHA/timeout; full universal pediatric cancer cure remains unverified.
AAP review describes multifactorial SIDS risk and states that individual deaths vary, making identification of one cause or universal mechanism difficult.
A small adult phase 1–2 trial reported restoration of islet function and insulin independence in some recipients, but participants needed immunosuppression and were 18–65 years old.

The HIE randomized trial tested a neonatal treatment and found no benefit on death/neurodevelopmental impairment. It provides context for disability prevention, but does not investigate or substantiate a birth biomarker predicting all cerebral palsy.
A 2026 preprint reports one expanded-access AAV9-GLB1 treatment in a child with one metabolic disease, a narrow author-reported result rather than universal platform validation.
A specific pediatric JIA stem-cell-transplantation clinical-trial page was located, but the opened primary page was unreadable; exact outcomes cannot be assessed here.
Randomized MOMS follow-up supports selected functional benefits of prenatal myelomeningocele surgery, but this is invasive, condition-specific surgery.
Adult donor-kidney Treg pilot provides narrow feasibility/safety evidence, while full withdrawal was prohibited; an ongoing pediatric study compares immunosuppression regimens rather than tolerance.

notes: All nine retained positive/context URLs independently reopened with actual title/topic/result passages matched.
NCI evidence synthesis narrowed to background-only after linked primary trial passage failed; no disproof of established CAR-T indication is implied.
HIE trial is background for CP prediction, not a birth-biomarker goal/result. Ongoing pediatric transplant registry supports planned comparison only; adult Treg pilot remains distinct.
Islet evidence is adult, immunosuppressed, small interim analysis; GM1 gene-transfer evidence is single-child unreviewed author report. Every source-supported claim is page-specific.
